_comment: Copy to ~/.config/peasant/mcp.json for servers you always want, or to
.peasant/mcp.json inside a repository for servers specific to it. The
project file wins by name, so a repository can replace a global server
without disabling it everywhere. Run 'peasant mcp' to see what loaded.
This is the same shape every other MCP client uses, so a block can be
copied from an existing configuration without translation.

_stdio_example._comment: A local server, spoken to over its stdin and stdout.

_comment: A real one, translated from a Claude Code configuration. See
docs/mcp.md for the translation table and a caveat about prebuilt
alwaysAllow names the server's OWN tool names, or "*" for all of
them. It is needed because most servers declare readOnlyHint on
nothing, so peasant treats everything as mutating and prompts before
every query. The write operations are deliberately left off.
A remote server over Streamable HTTP. https is required unless the
host is loopback: headers here may carry a token, and a token must
not cross a network in plaintext.
